note: Source of truth for Tobi's 12 Sep requests. Rendered to docs/TOBI-12SEP-CHANGES.md.

items.title: Chambers subscribe — separate pricing
items.requested: Chambers should be able to subscribe, with their own price system distinct from individual lawyers. Most competitor sites only serve lawyers + clients.
items.decision: Per member lawyer (seat-based) — uncertain, confirm with Tobi (→ Q1).

alternatives.why_rejected: Under-prices firms with many lawyers; Tobi framed it per member lawyer (still to confirm — Q1).

items.title: Tiered pricing (silver / premium)
items.requested: Tiers where premium gates the important features.
items.decision: Three-tier ladder Free → Silver → Premium; premium gates the important features; silver's exact contents deferred to Tobi's note (→ C21).
items.build_note: Silver/Free/Premium tier ladder (`lib/directory/publishing.ts` tier map + role ordering) wired into plans/pricing.

alternatives.why_rejected: Transcript says three; a middle tier is the upsell step and matches the 3 lawyer / 3 client / 1 firm plan shape.

items.title: Featured / prioritised profile placement
items.requested: Paid profiles get priority; they show up on the site ranked first.
items.decision: Build both — rank featured-first in search results and show a visible Featured badge on the card. Homepage featured section stays.
items.build_note: Featured-first ranking — `.order('is_featured', desc)` in `getLawyers` + `getChambers` (`lib/directory/api.ts`) and a visible Featured badge on cards.

alternatives.why_rejected: A badge without ordering is decoration — ranking is the part users pay for.

items.title: Enterprise price ₦3–5M/annum
items.requested: Enterprise (law firm) price bigger than ₦155k individual — around ₦3–5M per annum.
items.decision: Same as chamber — enterprise = chamber/law firm, one price. Exact annual figure still needs Tobi (→ Q9).

items.title: Post caps ~3/month + paid extras
items.requested: Cap publishing at ~3 posts/month; publishing extra posts costs a set amount (added revenue).
items.decision: Free: 1 post total → Premium: 3/month → extra posts = one-off Paystack payment. Both the free→paid funnel and the monthly cap.
items.build_note: Post-credit system: `lib/directory/publishing.ts` quota model + `20261016000002_post_caps_and_credits.sql` (free 1 total, paid 3/mo, extra = one-off Paystack credits) + `PublishQuotaBanner` in the publish flow.

alternatives.why_rejected: No revenue ceiling and no recurring reason to subscribe; caps create the paid-extras line.

items.title: One free article → premium to continue
items.requested: Give one free article; the next time they want to publish, require a premium subscription.
items.decision: Merged into C05 — the free allowance is the one-free-article funnel. No separate build.
items.build_note: Merged into C05 — the free allowance *is* the one-free-article funnel.

items.title: Back-end article publishing, editorial-gated
items.requested: Lawyers publish articles from their backend onto the Lawyard site, subject to editorial review.
items.decision: Gap was surfacing published articles on the directory — build out /directory/insights so articles appear there too, not only on WordPress. Publishing flow itself stays. Revisit in the WordPress-exit migration.
items.build_note: `/directory/insights` no longer a stub — published articles surface there through `getPublishedArticles`.

alternatives.why_rejected: Lawyard is exiting WordPress; the directory feed has to stand alone.

items.title: 1-min intro video — premium-only, self-hosted
items.requested: Premium subscribers can offer a 1-minute intro video hosted on our own backend (not free tier); factor cloud-storage cost into pricing.
items.decision: Both — premium-gated intro video that accepts either a self-hosted upload or an external URL (YouTube/Vimeo). Storage cost is trivial; bandwidth drives the model.
items.build_note: Premium intro video: `20261016000004_intro_videos_bucket.sql` (storage bucket) + `upload-intro-video.ts` action + `IntroVideoField` (upload **or** external URL), tier-gated.

alternatives.why_rejected: A paid feature needs an asset we control; firms with existing YouTube still get the URL path.
Friction for firms that already host video; cost is bandwidth, not storage.

items.title: Lawyard Lens courses + subscriber discount
items.requested: Host courses (e.g. AI governance ₦200k), discounted to ₦150k for directory subscribers — cross-sell.
items.decision: Thin, bespoke in the Next.js app — no WordPress. Course table + listing + Paystack checkout + subscriber discount; full LMS later only if it proves out.
items.build_note: Lawyard Lens: `20261016000006_lens_courses.sql` (courses + enrollments, AI Governance ₦200k/₦150k seeded), `courses.ts`, `/lens` + `/lens/[slug]` with Paystack checkout and server-side subscriber discount; enrollment handled in webhook + `verifyPayment`.

alternatives.why_rejected: Direction is off WordPress and AI-written bespoke over plugins.

items.title: Profile picture only (restrict uploads)
items.requested: Individuals upload only their profile picture (no free image galleries); note law firms may want more images/branding.
items.decision: Keep the gallery; enforce plan caps — free 3 / premium 6 — plus a higher cap for law firms. No blanket 'profile picture only'. Add image validation. Overrides Tobi's instinct: photos convert.
items.build_note: Gallery caps enforced by tier (free 3 / premium 6, higher for law firms) + image type/size validation.

alternatives.why_rejected: Deliberately overridden — photos convert; restriction moved to plan caps + image validation.

items.title: Chamber page — hours, FAQs, website, video, images
items.requested: Chamber page should have working-hours control, FAQs, website link, presentation video, and images.
items.decision: Full parity — extend chambers with working_hours, faqs, gallery_images, intro_video_url (website already exists), reusing the lawyer editors.
items.build_note: Full chamber parity: `20261016000005_chambers_parity.sql` reusing the lawyer editors, plus matching display sections on the public chamber page.

alternatives.why_rejected: Duplicated UI and parity drift; reusing the lawyer editors keeps one code path.

items.title: Private pricing option
items.requested: Allow a 'private' pricing option (hide price on the profile).
items.decision: Toggle hides the number, keeps the section → shows 'Contact for pricing'. Keeps the inquiry CTA while honouring the privacy ask.
items.build_note: `20261016000001_add_hide_price_to_lawyers.sql` + toggle in `LawyerForm` → profile shows 'Contact for pricing' instead of the number.

alternatives.why_rejected: Kills the inquiry CTA; hiding the number keeps the section working.

items.title: Remove 'link to directory' attribution
items.requested: Remove the 'link to directory' attribution/badge.
items.decision: Undecided — parked. 'Link Directory' is a plan feature (external links); no 'Powered by Lawyard' attribution found. Intent unclear → confirm with Tobi (→ Q10).

alternatives.option: Remove the Link Directory plan feature
alternatives.why_rejected: Not yet decided — depends on whether Tobi meant the feature or an attribution badge (Q10).

items.title: Rename booking → 'Service Request'
items.requested: Rename the feature to 'Service Request' — clients ask for services.
items.decision: New structured feature — not a rename of Inquiries. Captures service type, scope, budget; payable; entry point to the paid booking flow (C15). Inquiries stay as the free contact form.
items.build_note: `20261016000003_service_requests.sql` + `service-requests.ts` + `ServiceRequestForm` — structured service type / scope / budget request.

alternatives.why_rejected: Inquiries are the free contact form; service requests are structured and payable — different objects.

items.title: Bookings must be paid (no off-platform)
items.requested: Prevent free bookings that let the conversation move off-platform ('I don't want this to be a tracing cabinet').
items.decision: Client pays a booking fee to Lawyard via Paystack before the slot is confirmed. Chosen over routing the lawyer's consultation fee — keeps Lawyard charging for its own service, avoids handling client legal money and escrow obligations, and is the simplest build. Fee amount = Tobi (→ Q11).
items.build_note: Service requests are payable (Paystack booking fee to Lawyard before the slot is confirmed); no off-platform free bookings.

alternatives.option: Route the lawyer's consultation fee through Lawyard
alternatives.why_rejected: Payment-intermediary/escrow exposure and handling client legal money; charging for our own booking service is simpler and cleaner.

items.title: No Calendly / external calendar
items.requested: Do not integrate Calendly or an external calendar.
items.decision: Hide UI only — remove the LawyerForm field + the profile display; keep the calendly_url column in the DB (no destructive migration).
items.build_note: Calendly UI hidden from `LawyerForm` + lawyer profile display; `calendly_url` column kept.

alternatives.why_rejected: Destructive migration with no upside; hiding the UI is reversible.

items.title: Chamber site-admin role + PR publishing
items.requested: A chamber subscribes and gets a site administrator who manages the chamber page and publishes PR/announcements (e.g. IPO work) to the directory.
items.decision: Chamber-side role — the chamber gets one or more users with login who manage the chamber page + publish PR/announcement posts to the directory. Multiple users per chamber.
items.build_note: `20261016000007_chamber_admins.sql` — multi-user chamber admin role (owner/admin, RLS-managed, creator auto-registers as owner) + `press-releases.ts` publishing (editorial-gated via Slack) + dashboard 'Announcements & Press' + PRs on the public chamber page (excluded from the main Insights feed).

alternatives.why_rejected: Firms have staff turnover, and PR publishing needs a non-owner role.

items.title: Dashboard cleanup (bookmarks, history)
items.requested: Change the dashboard — remove bookmarks (not for client receipts); revisit the subscription/history section.
items.decision: Keep Bookmarks for both roles — a lawyer saving a peer is valid (referrals, co-counsel, benchmarking). Fix the confusion with clarity, not deletion: rename to 'Saved Lawyers'. Also clean up the subscription/history section.
items.build_note: Bookmarks kept for both roles, renamed 'Saved Lawyers' (sidebar, mobile nav, page title); subscription/history duplication cleaned up.

alternatives.why_rejected: Lawyer-to-lawyer saving is a real use case (referrals, co-counsel, benchmarking); clarity beats deletion.

items.title: Move to AWS
items.requested: Move infrastructure to AWS (a feature is getting heavy usage).
items.decision: Keep building with Supabase. If Shefiu insists on DigitalOcean, self-host Supabase on DO (code unchanged). No full migration off Supabase — 66 files are coupled to the SDK: auth, createClient, RLS, Storage.

alternatives.why_rejected: 66 files coupled to supabase-js — auth, createClient, RLS, Storage; self-host Supabase on DO if Shefiu insists.

items.title: Currency — Naira for Nigeria
items.requested: Naira for Nigeria; foreign listings need handling.
items.decision: NGN end-to-end — strip the hardcoded $ (3 layers: pricing fallback, getPlans() formatting, Price component), format as ₦, use Tobi's real NGN prices. Plus a foreign-listing decision.
items.build_note: `lib/currency.ts` NGN formatter end-to-end — hardcoded `$` removed from pricing fallback, `getPlans()` formatting and the `Price` component; foreign-listing handling noted.

alternatives.why_rejected: Buyers are Nigerian; NGN is the market and the payment rail already settles in NGN.

items.title: Silver category (which items stay/add)
items.requested: Tobi to send a note on which items to retain in the silver category and which to add.
items.decision: Draft a proposed silver feature set ourselves (middle tier between Free and Premium, derived from existing plan features) and send it to Tobi to react to — rather than waiting blank.

alternatives.why_rejected: A drafted proposal gives him something to react to instead of a blank page.

items.title: Generate a reviewable design pass
items.requested: Can you generate something for me to review — I'll review and send you notes next week.
items.decision: Build & ship the changes; Tobi reviews via voice recordings for the next round. No separate design-pass stage — this checklist is the build spec.
items.build_note: This checklist + the build pass *is* the deliverable — Tobi reviews via voice notes for the next round.

alternatives.why_rejected: Tobi reviews voice notes on a real build faster than a static prototype.

items.title: Rename 'Chamber' → 'Law Firm'
items.requested: Switch the product term 'Chamber' to 'Law Firm' throughout (raised during C01/C04).
items.decision: UI labels only — user-facing text says 'Law Firm'; keep the chambers table + /directory/chamber/* routes as-is internally.
items.build_note: UI labels switched to 'Law Firm' via centralized `TERMS` (`lib/constants.ts`) across nav, dashboard, forms, pricing and help; `chambers` table + `/directory/chamber/*` routes unchanged.

alternatives.option: Rename the chambers table and /directory/chamber routes too
alternatives.why_rejected: Churn across RLS, migrations and links for zero user-visible gain.
